svg.title: Interpreting scientific claims about factors associated with autism
svg.desc: Three levels: causal evidence in a particular setting, statistical associations without established causation, and unsupported or disproven claims. Estimates are population-level and do not imply parental blame.
svg.text: How strongly are different claims supported?

g.text: Established causal link in a defined context
Example: prenatal exposure to certain teratogenic medicines,
with important qualifications on dose, indication and other factors.
Parental age, some pregnancy complications and air pollution.
Findings need replication and assessment of confounding.
Causal explanation not supported or disproven
High-quality studies and WHO reviews do not support the claim
that routine childhood vaccinations cause autism.

svg.text: Population risk estimates do not assign blame to a family.
An educational framework, not an individual risk calculator.
